status_summary: The rescission the Mandate asks for was satisfied before 2025-01-20: the February 2023 proposed rule was withdrawn in a document published 2024-12-30, and a later October 2024 proposal on contraceptive coverage was withdrawn on 2025-01-15. No rulemaking curtailing the exemptions was found since 2025-01-20. On 2025-08-13 the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, in a case where the federal defendants and an intervenor defended the rules, vacated the Trump-era religious and moral exemption rules as arbitrary and capricious; an appeal is pending in the Third Circuit, which heard argument on 2026-07-07, with the federal government's counsel defending the exemptions; no appellate ruling was found as of 2026-10-18.

timeline.event: The Eastern District of Pennsylvania (No. 17-4540) entered judgment for Pennsylvania and New Jersey on their arbitrary and capricious claims and vacated the Religious Exemption Rule and the Moral Exemption Rule; judgment went to the federal defendants and the intervenor on the statutory authority and notice-and-comment claims.

title: Keep contraceptive mandate religious and moral exemptions; rescind 2023 proposal
uncertainties: Both withdrawal documents were opened on federalregister.gov in review: the 2024-12-30 document withdraws the February 2023 proposed rules (effective 2024-12-23), and the 2025-01-15 document withdraws the October 2024 proposed rules on contraceptive coverage. Both predate or fall at the edge of the period and are not counted as events; the 2025-01-15 withdrawal was signed 2025-01-13 under the prior administration. The 2025-08-13 district court order was read through a university litigation tracker copy. A news report (OSV News, 2025-12-15) says the intervenor, the Little Sisters of the Poor, filed the appeal on 2025-12-12; whether the federal government also appealed was not found, though a National Catholic Register (CNA) report says its counsel argued in support of the exemptions on 2026-07-07. The Third Circuit argument rests on news reports rather than the court's docket or calendar, and any ruling was not verified. The stage reflects that the exemptions the Mandate seeks to keep were vacated during the period while the rescission it requested had already occurred before the period. Primary-source lift 2026-10-18: the district court order was read as a PDF hosted by the Georgetown tracker (vacatur; judgment for defendants on statutory authority and notice-and-comment claims; other claims dismissed at plaintiffs' request). The Third Circuit argument date of 2026-07-07 is given by a National Catholic Register (CNA) report of 2026-07-08 and a Deseret News report; the Washington Examiner link formerly listed for the argument returned an unrelated page when opened and was removed. The reports say counsel for the federal government defended the exemptions at the argument, which indicates the government also participates in the appeal, but the appeal docket number and the identity of every appellant were not found. No Third Circuit opinion was found; the court's own opinion archive was not searched directly (one web search only), so a very recent ruling cannot be excluded. Whether any stay of the vacatur was sought or granted was not found.
